note: Hand-curated K-12 education analysis of HB2, New Hampshire's omnibus budget policy trailer, for the 2021, 2023, and 2025 budget cycles. Candidates came from relevance-term matching over every extracted section (see working/.../hb2/{year}/); a human pass kept the education sections, added three sections the matcher missed (flagged hand_added), and logged every exclusion. Roll-call votes are recorded on HB2 AS A WHOLE - a vote for or against the trailer is never a vote on one section, and must not be presented as one.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; Acceptance of Gifts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let the department of education accept private gifts and grants for department purposes with Governor and Council approval for the biennium.

relevant_sections.heading: Certain Differential Aid Calculations; Fiscal Year 2022
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let districts use their higher pre-pandemic or pandemic-year enrollment count for fiscal 2022 aid, so pandemic enrollment drops would not cut adequacy grants.

relevant_sections.heading: Conditional Differential Aid Calculation For Pupils Eligible for a Free or Reduced Price Meal; Fiscal Year 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Kept free-and-reduced-meal counts (and the aid tied to them) from collapsing in fiscal 2023 if pandemic conditions continued - a conditional hold-harmless for differentiated aid.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Relief Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created relief funding (RSA 198:40-e): an extra $600 per free-and-reduced-price-meal pupil in districts where at least 48 percent of pupils qualify, layered onto adequacy aid for the poorest districts.

relevant_sections.heading: Additional Aid to Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let a school district call a special meeting to decide how to budget any adjustment in its education aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Transfer; Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Moved $35 million of education trust fund surplus into a restricted account to pay the new relief funding in fiscal years 2022 and 2023.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; State Maintenance of Equity; Biennium Ending June 30, 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Directed the education department to certify compliance with the federal ARPA 'maintenance of equity' rule protecting high-poverty districts' shares of state aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $3 million from the education trust fund for a statewide student data collection and reporting system - the state's education-data infrastructure.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote what the education trust fund may pay for - adequacy grants, the homeowners' property tax relief program, and the new education freedom accounts among them.

relevant_sections.heading: Transfer; Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Transferred $1 million a year from the education trust fund to the public school infrastructure fund in each year of the biennium.

relevant_sections.heading: Public School Infrastructure Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the public school infrastructure fund statute (RSA 198:15-y) - the school security and infrastructure account funded by state surpluses.

relevant_sections.heading: Repeal
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the scheduled sunset of the public school infrastructure fund, making the fund permanent.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Tax Credit Scholarship Organizations; 2027
relevant_sections.plain_language: Conforming change to the education tax credit scholarship statute for the interest-and-dividends repeal: individuals' I&D-tax credits for scholarship-organization donations end with the tax in 2027 (later 2025).

relevant_sections.heading: Education Tax Credit Scholarship Organizations; 2027
relevant_sections.plain_language: Companion conforming change to the scholarship-organization award rules for the same repeal.

relevant_sections.heading: Meals and Rooms Tax; Disposition of Revenue; Fund Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the meals and rooms tax distribution, fixing the education trust fund's share of that revenue while creating the municipal revenue fund (the tax mechanics live in the property-taxes packet).

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; State Commission on Human Rights; Right to Freedom From Discrimination in Public Workplaces and Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: The companion civil-rights half of the teaching ban: a new 'right to freedom from discrimination in public workplaces and education' under the human rights commission (RSA 354-A:29 and following), giving the banned-concepts rule an enforcement path including teacher-license discipline.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Prohibition on Teaching Discrimination
relevant_sections.plain_language: The 'divisive concepts' teaching ban as enacted: no public school pupil shall be taught or compelled to express belief in a list of concepts about the superiority or inferiority of any group (new RSA 193:40) - the classroom-content restriction later struck down in part by a federal court and repealed in the 2025 trailer's DEI rewrite's shadow.

relevant_sections.heading: Community College System of New Hampshire; Dual and Concurrent Enrollment Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the dual and concurrent enrollment program (RSA 188-E:25-29): high school students earn community-college credit in STEM and career courses with the state paying tuition - the main high-school-to-career bridge program.

relevant_sections.heading: School Building Aid; Annual Grant for Leased Space
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended annual school building aid lease grants to more kinds of district lease arrangements, including space leased from other districts and municipalities.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Ten Year Plan for Grant Projects
relevant_sections.plain_language: Required the department of education to maintain a 10-year school facilities plan ranking potential school building aid projects.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Kindergarten Adequate Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made full-day kindergarten adequacy grants a standing charge on the education trust fund every year, ending the keno-revenue-dependent formula.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $1.9 million to top up fiscal 2021 kindergarten and adequacy grant payments.

relevant_sections.heading: School Planning Committees; Vacancies
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how vacancies on cooperative and area school planning committees and school boards are filled - district governance mechanics.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $30 million from the education trust fund for school building aid on new projects - the first new-project money after a decade-long moratorium era.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Tax Revenue; Fiscal Year 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the statewide education property tax (SWEPT) for fiscal year 2023: the rate is set to raise $263 million instead of the usual $363 million target - a one-year, $100 million cut in the local school tax the state counts as its aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Supplemental Education Payment; Fiscal Year 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Guaranteed no municipality's total education grant would fall because of the SWEPT cut: the state makes up any decrease with a supplemental payment.

relevant_sections.heading: System of Care for Children's Mental Health; Duties of the Commissioner of the Department of Education; Reference Change
relevant_sections.plain_language: Folded the department of education into the children's mental health system of care plan - schools as a delivery point for children's behavioral health.

relevant_sections.heading: Medicaid to Schools Program; Fiscal Committee Approval of Supplemental Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let the Medicaid-to-schools program accept extra federal money mid-biennium with fiscal committee approval - the funding stream for school-based health services.

relevant_sections.heading: New Chapter; Education Freedom Accounts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the education freedom account (EFA) program (new RSA 194-F): state adequacy money follows a student out of public school to private, religious, or home education expenses, paid from the education trust fund through a scholarship organization - the biggest school-choice change of the period.

relevant_sections.heading: Duty of Parent; Compulsory Attendance by Pupil
relevant_sections.plain_language: Amended the compulsory-attendance statute so participation in the EFA program satisfies a child's school-attendance duty - the conforming change that makes the program legal schooling.

relevant_sections.heading: Career and Technical Education; Dual and Concurrent Enrollment Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the dual and concurrent enrollment program to career and technical education center students in grades 10 through 12.

relevant_sections.heading: Regional Career and Technical Education; Dual and Concurrent Enrollment Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Doubled the funded dual/concurrent enrollment courses per student (from 2 to 4 in each of grades 10, 11, and 12).

relevant_sections.heading: Repeals; Advanced Manufacturing Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the advanced manufacturing education advisory council and partnership statutes (RSA 188-E:21-24) - a CTE-adjacent program taken off the books.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Department of Education; The Commission on New Hampshire Civics; Commission Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the commission on New Hampshire civics inside the department of education - the body charged with building the state's civics-education program.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; Commission on New Hampshire Civics
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $1 million to the civics commission, including a New Hampshire civics textbook project.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Department of Education; Higher Education; Recruitment of Educators
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created an educator recruitment program: stipends and grants for academic residencies and alternative certification pathways, aimed at the teacher shortage.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; ARPA and ESSER Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let discretionary federal ARPA/ESSER money fund the educator recruitment stipends.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a computer science and STEM administrator position in the department of education.

relevant_sections.heading: New Chapter; Computer Science Educator Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the computer science educator program (new RSA 200-O): tuition-reimbursement incentives for teachers earning computer science credentials - the trailer's main classroom-technology investment.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriations; Department of Education; Computer Science Professional Development
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $500,000 for computer science professional development credentials for certified educators.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Public School Infrastructure Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $10 million from the education trust fund into the public school infrastructure fund for school construction and safety projects.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Appropriations Reductions; Education Freedom Accounts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Reduced the education trust fund appropriation earmarked for education freedom accounts by $10 million in each year of the biennium, an accounting true-up to actual enrollment.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Re-enacted the education trust fund statute, restating everything the fund may pay for - adequacy grants, homeowners' property tax relief, EFAs, court-ordered placements, and school building aid among them.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Education of Children Placed in Homes for Children, Health Care Facilities, or State Institutions; Episode of Treatment
relevant_sections.plain_language: Defined 'episode of treatment' placements for children placed by DHHS in facilities - the definition the special-education payment sections hang on.

relevant_sections.heading: Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Changed special education state aid so districts are reimbursed for costs above 3.5 times the state average per-pupil cost - the 'catastrophic aid' threshold that decides when the state steps in.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Special Education; State Aid; Rulemaking by State Board of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Gave the state board of education rulemaking authority for paying episode-of-treatment costs.

relevant_sections.heading: Liability for Children with Disabilities in Certain Court Ordered Placements
relevant_sections.plain_language: Shifted liability for certain court-ordered placements of children with disabilities, defining when the state rather than the school district pays.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Court Ordered Placements
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $9.2 million from the education trust fund for court-ordered placement costs.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Funding for Renovation and Expansion; CTE
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the career and technical education renovation-funding statute the CTE center projects run through.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; Appropriation; CTE Renovation Projects; Sugar River Valley Regional Technical Center
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $12.5 million from the education trust fund for the Sugar River Valley career and technical education renovation project.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $7.6 million from the education trust fund for the Winnisquam regional CTE renovation project.

relevant_sections.heading: Cost of an Opportunity for an Adequate Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the cost of an adequate education (RSA 198:40-a): base per-pupil aid rises to $4,100 with larger add-ons for free-and-reduced-lunch pupils, special education, and English learners - the formula rewrite the whole 2023 education budget turned on.

relevant_sections.heading: Annual Adjustment; Relief Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Re-enacted the annual adjustment: adequacy aid amounts rise 2 percent automatically every year starting July 2024.

relevant_sections.heading: Extraordinary Need Grants; 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote extraordinary need grants for 2023 - extra aid scaled to a town's equalized property value per pupil, targeting the towns with the weakest tax bases.

relevant_sections.heading: Extraordinary Need Grants; 2025
relevant_sections.plain_language: Set the 2025-and-after version of extraordinary need grants, extending the property-poor-town aid formula.

relevant_sections.heading: Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how each municipality's total education grant is determined, including hold-harmless rules so no town's grant falls below prior levels while the new formula phases in.

relevant_sections.heading: Chartered Public Schools; Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Raised chartered public school per-pupil funding: adequacy amounts plus an additional grant, with the amount indexed going forward - the charter funding statute's biggest rewrite of the period.

relevant_sections.heading: Repeal; Third Grade Reading Accountability
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the third-grade reading accountability data requirement from the statewide assessment statute (RSA 193-C) - a piece of the testing regime removed.

relevant_sections.heading: State Maintenance of Equity
relevant_sections.plain_language: Amended the 2021 maintenance-of-equity provision so any such aid distributes as an education grant to districts and charter schools.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Distribution to Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Fixed the education trust fund's share of the business profits tax at 41 percent of revenue - replacing the old 'increase attributable to' formula with a straight statutory split.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Distribution to Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Fixed the education trust fund's share of the business enterprise tax at 41 percent of revenue, the same straight split.

relevant_sections.heading: Medicaid to Schools Program; Fiscal Committee Approval of Supplemental Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the Medicaid-to-schools supplemental-funding authority through the 2025 biennium.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education; Kindergarten Adequate Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $315,700 from the education trust fund for new full-day kindergarten adequacy grants.

relevant_sections.heading: The sum of $150,000 is hereby appropriated for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023, to the department of education for the purpose of contracting with the National Student Clearinghouse Student Tracker Program for each public school district in New Hampshire
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $150,000 to contract with the National Student Clearinghouse to track every district's graduates into college and careers - an outcomes-measurement investment.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Math Learning Communities Program in Public Secondary Schools; Structure
relevant_sections.plain_language: Required annual reporting on the math learning communities program partnering community colleges with high schools.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Community College System of New Hampshire
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $200,000 a year to continue the math learning communities program.

relevant_sections.heading: Duties
relevant_sections.plain_language: Charged a study committee with examining how expanded free-and-reduced-price-meal eligibility (SNAP categorical eligibility, Medicaid data) changes the pupil counts that drive state education aid.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; Commission to Study Hospitality and Tourism Education in New Hampshire
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a commission to study hospitality and tourism education - the industry-pathways study that also arrived as a standalone bill (SB37).

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education; Adult Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $500,000 for grants to adult education programs - the second-chance diploma track.

relevant_sections.heading: Career and Technical Education Incentive Grant
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the career and technical education incentive grant to pay transportation costs that keep sending-district students out of regional CTE centers.

relevant_sections.heading: Career and Technical Education Incentive Grant; Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $4 million for the CTE transportation incentive grant program.

relevant_sections.heading: Findings; Children's Mental Health
relevant_sections.plain_language: Findings on children's mental health: schools named as the daily front line of the behavioral-health crisis.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education; Children's Mental Health; MTSS-B Framework
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $900,000 for the multi-tiered system of supports for behavior (MTSS-B) framework in schools.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Freedom Accounts; Contingency
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made the education freedom account expansion's effective date contingent on program participation certification - the mechanics attached to 2025's removal of the EFA income cap (2025, 75) that opened the program to every family.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Education Freedom Accounts; Application for an Education Freedom Account
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let an EFA student leave the program and re-enroll in public school on notice to the scholarship organization - exit mechanics for the expanded program.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; School Money; Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Amended the education trust fund's purpose list, including how court-ordered placement costs are paid.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; School Money; Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Capped the education trust fund's balance: any surplus over $20 million at the close of a biennium is swept into the general fund - money that once stayed dedicated to schools.

relevant_sections.heading: Chartered Public Schools; Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the chartered public school tuition payment schedule (30/40/30 percent installments on enrollment counts).

relevant_sections.heading: New Subparagraph; Chartered Public Schools; Funding
relevant_sections.plain_language: Set special payment rules for the Virtual Learning Academy Charter School based on estimated full-time enrollment.

relevant_sections.heading: Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Moved the final determination of education grants to October 1 and guaranteed each municipality at least 95 percent of its estimated grant.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the education trust fund's share of the business profits tax from 41 percent to 39 percent, keeping more business tax revenue in the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the education trust fund's share of the business enterprise tax from 41 percent to 39 percent.

relevant_sections.heading: Tobacco Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the tobacco tax split: 39 percent of tobacco revenue to the education trust fund, the rest to the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Tax on Transfer of Real Property; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the real estate transfer tax split: 39 percent to the education trust fund, the rest to the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Annual Adjustment
relevant_sections.plain_language: Delayed the annual 2 percent inflation adjustment of per-pupil adequacy aid to July 2026 - a pause in the automatic growth of state school aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Extraordinary Need Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Re-enacted the extraordinary need grant formula - the extra aid tied to a town's equalized property value per pupil.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Fiscal Capacity Disparity Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created fiscal capacity disparity aid: up to $1,250 extra per pupil for municipalities with less than $1 million of equalized property value per pupil, phasing out by $1.6 million - aid aimed squarely at property-poor towns.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how each municipality's education grant is computed to fold in the new fiscal capacity disparity aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Instruction in National and State History, Government, and Civics
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the required civics instruction statute (RSA 189:11): the locally developed civics competency assessment and the naturalization-test requirement for graduation - the testing piece of the civics program.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriations; Department of Education; Computer Science Professional Development
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the 2023 computer science professional-development appropriations' availability.

relevant_sections.heading: Public School Infrastructure Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let the public school infrastructure commission approve fund expenditures without fiscal committee sign-off.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Special Education; Program Approval, Monitoring, and Corrective Action
relevant_sections.plain_language: Ordered an independent, nationally recognized audit of the state's special education program approval and monitoring system - the oversight response to exploding special-education costs.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Restructured special education state aid administration and reimbursement - the catastrophic-cost aid that shields local budgets.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the funding rule for statewide special education programs.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Education Freedom Accounts; Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let unused EFA funds roll over quarter-to-quarter and year-to-year until withdrawal or graduation.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Medicaid to Schools Program; Termination
relevant_sections.plain_language: Added a statewide termination trigger to the Medicaid-to-schools program if federal or state policy conflicts with parental control of children's medical services.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; Prohibition on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
relevant_sections.plain_language: The statewide companion: the same DEI prohibition applied to every state agency and political subdivision (new RSA 21-I:112 and following), which reaches school districts as public employers.

relevant_sections.heading: New Subdivision; Prohibition on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Public Schools
relevant_sections.plain_language: Prohibited diversity, equity, and inclusion programs in public schools (new RSA 186:71 and following): no DEI offices, officers, trainings, or DEI-based hiring or contracting in schools, with enforcement through the department of education - the 2025 trailer's biggest education-policy section.

relevant_sections.heading: Legislative Declaration of Authority Regarding Public Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Declared the legislature's position on the Claremont school-funding rulings - asserting that defining and funding an adequate education is the legislature's prerogative - while the ConVal litigation over adequacy amounts and the SWEPT remains in the courts.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adult Education; Establishment of Adult High School Education Program
relevant_sections.plain_language: Restated the adult education program statute as the adult high school education program for residents 16 and older.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $400,000 a year from the education trust fund for adult high school education programs.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Student and Teacher Information Protection and Privacy; Student Privacy
relevant_sections.plain_language: Narrowed the student-privacy statute's protected 'workforce information' definition (RSA 189:68) - part of the student-data layer.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; District Taxes; Reports Required; Cities and School Districts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made the education and revenue departments jointly maintain school accounting standards - the books behind local school budgets and tax rates.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $1.5 million a year from the education trust fund for statewide student learning platforms - the state's classroom-technology line.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Cell Phone Use Policy
relevant_sections.plain_language: Required every school board and charter school to adopt a policy governing student cell phones and other personal electronic devices in school - the statewide 'bell-to-bell' phone-policy mandate, with exceptions for IEPs, 504 plans, and medical needs.
